definition: A schematic image is a mentally organized spatial representation formed by assembling different kinds of visual and spatial information into a structured whole. In this context, it refers to the kind of internal layout or pattern that spatial processing helps build during thinking and problem-solving.

reasons: The packet supports only the phrase “spatial-schematic image” in a physics/child cognition context, not a standalone lexical sense for “schematic image.”

The definition adds unsupported generalizations about a mentally organized representation used in thinking and problem-solving; the packet only says spatial processing may help assemble diverse visual-spatial information into a spatial-schematic image.
The wording is broader and more interpretive than the source, which does not define the term as a structured whole or an internal layout/pattern.

The packet only states that spatial processing “may sub-serve the assembly of diverse sources of visual-spatial information into a spatial-schematic image,” which does not directly support the broader definition’s wording about a “mentally organized spatial representation,” “structured whole,” or an “internal layout or pattern.”

The definition generalizes the role of schematic images to “thinking and problem-solving,” but the packet’s discussion of problem-solving is specifically in the context of “physics problem-solving,” with no support for a general cognition/thinking definition beyond that setting.
